paragraphs.text: Cridhe is a small plane , whose land area is composed mostly of a single island . It was the setting of the novel The Cursed Land .
Cridhe was created by a being called the Maker and was home to humans and elves and various small animals. Life on Cridhe revolves around the Clan Tree, which is considered the heart of the plane.

While things were dark and miserable during the time the novel is set, the healed wizard Nazir had a prophetic vision of what the plane would look like 1000 years in the future. That future is depicted on the Plane card Inys Haen .

Cridhe - the eponymous main landmass of the plane of Cridhe Inys Haen - residence of the Heanish (the descendants of Haen ) in the central mountainous region The Blessing Stone The Clan Tree of Cridhe - containing all the plane's mana . Jedhian's Hill Nohrland - the areas north and east of Inys Haen controlled by the Nohrish. The Far clanholds - area on the edge of Nohrish territory northeast of Inys Haen, home to the four Far clans. The Far clanners were made up of Nohrish refugees and runaways that kept an uneasy peace with Inys Haen. The seal of the first Far clan was a mountain. The sigil of the third was three corbies. Caer Glammis - home of the fourth Far clan. Inys Nohr - residence of the Nohrish (the descendants of Nohr ) on the east coast The Moors - moorlands northeast of the Slicks The Slicks - the swampy hills bordering the moors. Located just past Caer Glammis, landslides following the Parting left it covered in oily bogs with pockets of quicksand. It is teeming with widowweed. The River Sobus - the icy river that flows through the Great Rending , the rift created by the Parting, northeast from Inys Haen to just past Inys Nohr at the mouth of the Sea of Sorrows. Two or three fisherman drown each year in its narrows, and their bodies are lost in the caverns that lay under the water. Raphos Falls - a waterfall east of Inys Haen, named after Raphos the blacksmith. The Westlands - the western coast of Cridhe island, where there is a secret entrance to Loch Prith. Loch Prith - an underground elvish paradise on the west coast
The Great Whirlpool - in the ocean south of the island
The Ribbon - in the ocean south of the island
The Sea of Sorrows - the sea to the northeast of the island
The Southern Isle - a small island and the only other known landmass on the plane.
The Sea of Swells - the sea to the southeast of the island
The Western Sea - the sea west of the island
Cridhe has one sun and one moon. Though its stars became erratic after the Parting, a few constellations are known:
The hunter, whose bright bow is made up of one green star and three red ones

On midsummer eve around 3043 AR , after being instigated by Malvos , the wizard Nohr destroyed the tree trying to become a planeswalker . When it was destroyed, the stability of the plane was violated. The ancient curse of the god who created this plane became true. The isle split in two, separating the Clan. Nohr and his descendants were cursed with madness.

Following the Parting, the plane was plunged into a climate crisis. Clouds immediately obscured the sun, creating a permanent daily twilight and nightly darkness. The plane's moon and stars were only visible around the spring equinox. Crops withered, livestock changed and died, and even the stars became unfixed in the sky. Nohrland, which had been forested with jungle for hundreds of years, withered and died, becoming a fungal forest as the weather turned cold. As time passed without the tree, the seasons grew increasingly erratic, leading to a cold period known as the Long Winter. Each spring, on the vernal equinox, the Keeper needed to manifest the Memory of spring, allowing it to take hold in the land and create another year of growth. The winter of Year 519 was so cold that trees exploded from their freezing sap and cattle froze overnight. By Year 520, the birthrate in Inys Nohr had dropped precipitously, to the point that infant mortality rose to 50%.

In Year 520, Keeper Aylith and Felonarch Nazir descendants of Haen and Nohr, mended the Clan Tree . In the following years, the tree grew quickly, returning the stars and the seasons to their regular cycles. By one thousand years later, the clan was reunited, Inys Nohr became a great city, and Inys Haen became a great pasture of farmland, orchards, and gardens.

As foretold by Haen , the Mending of the Clan Tree occurred when the lines of Haen and Nohr finally met. 520 years after the Parting, the Keeper Aylith used her powers to break the curse on Nazir . Together they spoke the litany of light and recreated the Clan Tree of Cridhe from the last existing acorn.
paragraphs.section: The Mending of the Clan Tree

paragraphs.text: The tree experiences intense mana showers.
paragraphs.section: The Mending of the Clan Tree

paragraphs.text: A holiday called Festival is celebrated each year on Midsummer Eve. All of Cridhe speaks a single common tongue. Inhabitants are known to wear a woven garment called a bhana, seemingly a form of bandana, cloak, or blanket. A decca is a unit of currency. Soldiers are known to play dice and cards for fun, and children play hide and find.

Nohrish cuisine was dictated by the meager resources of Nohrland. Eels were common fare, and meat-and-raisin pie was also eaten. The rich are known to enjoy sweets including honey cakes, and cream and honey pie, and custard tarts. Albions subsist on ardré.
Ale was considered rare and expensive, only drunk in the Tower of Inys Nohr. Most Nohrish drank perf, a mushroom sour mash. Haenish are known to enjoy hot, spiced wine.
Humans Mirkalbions or Albions, a type of blue-skinned humans
Birds Corbies Eagles Owls Parrots (extinct after the Parting ) Thatch hens, gray with black wings

Fish Eels, with purple skin, long jaws, and razor teeth. Preferring cold water, they appeared during the Long Winter. They swam in the moat of the Tower of Inys Nohr, infested the river, and ate most of the game fish left in Cridhe. Salmon
Frogs Bullfrogs (extinct after the Parting )
Horses (extinct after the Parting )

Insects Bees Butterflies Gnats Lumini, tiny fireflies created by Crephas that formed balls of light in perfect cooperation Moths with pale green wings spanning several feet Sea roaches Shield bugs, which grow large and hunt at night with serrated pincers and wide polished silver mirror eyes. During the day, they flatten themselves and turn their eyes black to capture the sun's meager heat. According to fisherfolk legend, if you see your reflection in a shield bug's eyes, he would eat you the next day. Termites

Makana, great burrowing lizardlike creatures created by Crephas . Unaffected by the cold, they have ghostly white skin, wedge-shaped heads, long teeth and claws, and small, blind red eyes. They roam Nohrland's lower elevations, adept tunnelers but unable to climb. They eat mostly carrion but preferred to hunt, using an acute sense of heat to locate their prey.
Shrouds , creatures that mimic clothing and kill using acid
Spiders , which can grow as large as cats and decorate their backs with found items. Crookspiders, which spin gold webs

Bitteroots, great leafless black vines that permeated the stonework of Inys Nohr. They are huge, with thick, curling trunks and a slick, glassy surface. They are cold to the touch and hard enough to deflect blades.
Cottonum, a natural fiber grown in Loch Prith that is used to make soft, warm fabrics that sooth injuries.
Crops Corn Grapes, used to make raisins and wine. Oats Potatoes Turnips, grown around Inys Haen
Flowers Daylily (extinct after the Parting ) Dog violet Lily Orchids Plum blossom Purple clover Sunflower (extinct after the Parting )

Fungus Ardré, a fungus eaten by the Albions. Before his madness, Crephas created the plant to make him less sensitive to the cold. Though he was unsuccessful, his tinkering with both its taste and effects allowed him to engineer the Albions to work the coal mines, so that he would never be cold again. Requiring a constant level of darkness, it can only be grown on north-facing crags populated by white minerals that maintain the fungus's properties. Its spores are considered stronger. Giant mushrooms that replaced the trees within Nohrland. Rubbery gray and brown, with massive blue puffballs that sprayed dark purple spores. Morels A cottony white fungus referred to as "the walking plague", which grew quickly on open wounds in Nohrland and slowly undulated in waves, known as "walking".
Herbs Haenish fennel Haenish lavender Rosemary Clove Sage Speedwell, an herb known to cure the walking plague. Thyme
Hiroo, used to make fishing nets
Lichen, in orange and yellow.
Stinkworts, which grow bright orange in Nohrland.
Trees Birch Cedar Elder Oak Rosewood Walnut

Widowweeds, large plants with pale, fleshy stalks and black, ruffled, hood-shaped heads. Any disturbance in the air near the plants causes them to emit a low whistle that sounds like a mourning woman. They are known to lure people into bogs to drown so that their roots can feed.

The walking plague was a significant cause of death in Nohrland after the Parting. It grew quickly on any open wounds and killed soon thereafter. It could be cured with speedwell. Pestilent fog was known to roll in from the sea, causing a coughing sickness known as the hack, which killed over weeks, causing its victims to foam pinkish saliva. After the Mending of the Clan Tree, Aylith and Nazir were able to cure these sicknesses.
